examples.en: The news introduced a new missile technology.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 미사일이 어떻게 날아가는지 배웠어요.
examples.en: In science class we learned how a missile flies.

examples.ko: 박물관에 오래된 미사일 모형이 전시되어 있어요.
examples.en: The museum has an old missile model on display.
The article said this missile is for defense.
I have a friend who works at a missile research institute.
Rockets and missiles are similar, but their uses differ.

explain: '로켓'은 우주로 가는 것에도 쓰지만 '미사일'은 목표물을 맞히도록 만든 무기에만 써요. 뉴스와 과학 기사에서 주로 보는 말이고 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 나와요.
explain_en: '로켓' also covers space launchers, but '미사일' is used only for weapons built to hit a target. You mostly see it in news and science articles, rarely in everyday talk.

examples.en: The Roman Empire existed a very long time ago.
I saw items from the imperial era at the museum.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 거대한 제국과 작은 나라의 이야기예요.
examples.en: The movie is about a huge empire and a small country.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 한때 아주 큰 제국이었어요.
examples.en: That country was once a very big empire.

examples.ko: 제국이 사라진 뒤에 새 나라가 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new country appeared after the empire disappeared.

examples.ko: 구한말 대한 제국 시대에는 사회가 많이 불안정했어요.
examples.en: Society was very unstable during the Korean Empire period in the late Joseon era.

explain: 일상 대화보다 역사 수업, 영화, 게임 이야기에서 더 자주 들려요. 왕이 다스리면 '왕국', 황제가 다스리면 '제국'이라고 구분해요. '대한제국'처럼 이름 안에 들어가면 붙여 써요.
explain_en: You will meet this word in history class, films and games more than in daily chat. A land ruled by a king is a '왕국' and one ruled by an emperor is a '제국'. Inside names such as '대한제국' it is written without a space.

examples.en: The teacher does not discriminate among students.
You must not discriminate against people because of age.
That shop treats customers unequally.
There was a time they treated someone differently for being foreign.
It hurts to hear discriminating words.

examples.ko: 누구도 차별할 수 없다고 법에 쓰여 있어요.
examples.en: The law says no one may be discriminated against.

explain: 사람을 이유 없이 다르게 대할 때 써요. 단순히 '구별하다'와 달리 불공평하다는 나쁜 뜻이 있어요. 당하는 쪽은 '차별을 받다'나 '차별당하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes treating people differently for no good reason. Unlike plain '구별하다', it carries a negative sense of unfairness. The person on the receiving end says '차별을 받다' or '차별당하다'.

examples.ko: 귀화 후에는 투표권도 생겨서 선거에 참여할 수 있어요.
examples.en: After naturalization you also get the right to vote and can take part in elections.
You have the right to vote from age eighteen.

examples.ko: 투표권을 가진 사람만 투표할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only people who hold the right to vote can vote.
There are elections in which foreigners have no right to vote.
Is there an age limit on the right to vote?
I brought my ID in order to exercise my right to vote.

explain: '선거권'과 비슷해서 바꿔 쓰기도 해요. 보통 '투표권을 행사하다'처럼 써요. 이때 '행사하다'는 '권리를 실제로 쓰다'라는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is similar to '선거권', and the two are sometimes interchanged. It is usually used as '투표권을 행사하다'. Here '행사하다' carries the feel of actually using a right.
